**`message_history` semantics** ([notes_spec.py:20-35](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/notes_spec.py#L20-L35)):
On every update, `NoteMessageUpdateSpec.perform_extra_deserialization` fetches the **pre-update** DB object (`old_obj = NoteMessage.objects.get(external_id=obj.external_id)`) and appends a snapshot of the *old* message to `obj.message_history["history"]` (a list) before the new message overwrites `obj.message`. Each history entry is a dict: `{"message": <old message text>, "created_by": {"username", "external_id"}, "edited_at": <now>, "created_at": <old modified_date>}`. Note the field names are misleading: `created_by`/`created_at` in a history entry actually refer to the **editor and the time of the previous version**, not the original author — `old_obj.created_by` is the message's original author (fixed per message) while `old_obj.modified_date` is when that prior version was last saved. This is only invoked on **update**, never on create, so `message_history` starts as `{}` for a new message and is only populated after ≥1 edit.

**Audit fields from `EMRBaseModel`** (`care/emr/models/base.py:8-27`, applies to both models):
- `history` (JSONField, default `{}`) — inherited but **unused** for notes; a `# TODO Handle historical data...` in `EMRUpdateMixin.perform_update` (`care/emr/api/viewsets/base.py:177`) confirms this generic history mechanism isn't implemented — notes instead built their own bespoke `message_history` field.
- `meta` (JSONField, default `{}`) — inherited, unused for notes.
- `created_by` / `updated_by` — FK to `users.User`, `SET_NULL`, nullable. Set automatically: `created_by`/`updated_by` on create (`EMRCreateMixin.perform_create`, base.py:97-98), `updated_by` on update (`EMRUpdateMixin.perform_update`, base.py:178). Serialized as `dict` via `cls.serialize_audit_users(mapping, obj)` in both read specs (notes_spec.py:49, thread_spec.py:37).
- Plus, from `BaseModel` (`care/utils/models/base.py:14-24`): `external_id` (UUID4, unique), `created_date`/`modified_date` (auto timestamps), `deleted` (soft-delete boolean, default `False`).

**None.** Neither `NoteThread` nor `NoteMessage` nor their resource specs define any `Choices`/enum class — confirmed by reading the full contents of [notes.py (model)](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/models/notes.py), [notes_spec.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/notes_spec.py), and [thread_spec.py](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/resources/notes/thread_spec.py) — no status field, no type field, no coded value of any kind exists on threads or messages.

### Behavioral rules and validations

1. **Thread creation — patient/encounter mismatch check** ([notes.py:80-84](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L80-L84)): `perform_create` sets `instance.patient` from the URL, then if `instance.encounter and instance.encounter.patient != instance.patient`, raises `ValidationError("Patient Mismatch")`. Verified by `test_create_thread_on_encounter_with_patient_mismatch` (test_notes_api.py).
2. **Message creation — thread-must-belong-to-patient check** ([notes.py:112-118](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L112-L118)): `get_thread_obj()` raises `ValidationError("Thread does not belong to the patient")` if `thread.patient_id != patient.id`. Verified by `test_list_notes_with_patient_thread_mismatch`, `test_get_note_details_with_patient_thread_mismatch`.
3. **Message creation — optional per-message encounter override with patient mismatch check** ([notes.py:120-127](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L120-L127)): if the create request body has an `encounter` key, it's resolved and if `encounter.patient != instance.thread.patient`, raises `ValidationError("Patient Mismatch")`. Otherwise `instance.encounter = encounter` (attribute set on an in-memory model instance — see issue below, since `NoteMessage` has no `encounter` DB field).
4. **Message retrieve/update — message-belongs-to-thread check**: `authorize_retrieve` ([notes.py:154-157](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L154-L157)) and `authorize_update` ([notes.py:145-150](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L145-L150)) both raise `ValidationError("Message does not belong to the thread")` if `model_instance.thread != thread` (thread resolved from URL). Verified by `test_get_note_details_with_invalid_thread`.
5. **"Cannot update message created by another user"** ([notes.py:145-146](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L145-L146)): `authorize_update` raises `PermissionDenied("Cannot Update Message Created by Other User")` if `self.request.user.id != model_instance.created_by_id` — this check applies **regardless of role/permission**, i.e., even a facility admin cannot edit someone else's message. No corresponding test exercises this exact message in `test_notes_api.py`, but the code path is unconditional (see AMBIGUITIES).
6. **Threads can be renamed**: `NoteThreadUpdateSpec` only inherits `title` (thread_spec.py:32-33) — `encounter` is excluded from update, so only `title` is updatable via `PUT`/`PATCH` on a thread. Verified by `test_update_thread`.
7. **Deletion**: **Not possible for either threads or messages.** Neither `NoteThreadViewSet` nor `NoteMessageViewSet` includes `EMRDestroyMixin` (only `EMRCreateMixin, EMRRetrieveMixin, EMRUpdateMixin, EMRListMixin` are mixed in, notes.py:31-45, 108-112) — there is no `destroy` action wired, so DELETE is not exposed on these routes.
8. **Ordering**:
   - Threads: `.order_by("-created_date")` (newest thread first) — `NoteThreadViewSet.get_queryset` (notes.py:106).
   - Messages: on `list` action, `.filter(thread=thread).order_by("-created_date")` (newest message first); on other actions (retrieve/update), `.order_by("-modified_date")` (notes.py:174-179).
9. **Filtering** (`NoteThreadFilters`, notes.py:26-28): `encounter` — `UUIDFilter` on `encounter__external_id`; `encounter_isnull` — custom `NullFilter` (`care/utils/filters/null_filter.py`) that filters `encounter__isnull=<bool>` when a boolean value is passed, no-op if `None`/absent. `NoteMessageViewSet` has **no `filterset_class`** — the only "filtering" for messages is the implicit `thread` scoping in `get_queryset`.
10. **Global visibility gate (both viewsets' `get_queryset`)**: if the user lacks `can_view_clinical_data` on the patient, the code falls back to checking a `?encounter=` query param — if present, requires `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` on that encounter, else raises `PermissionDenied("Permission denied to user")`. If no `?encounter=` param is present and patient-level view is denied, always `PermissionDenied` (notes.py:93-103, 163-171) — this **query param gate does not verify the referenced encounter is actually linked to any of the returned threads/messages**, it's purely a view-authorization side-channel (see SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES #3).
11. **Encounter completion blocks new clinical writes**: `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` (`care/security/authorization/encounter.py:97-105`) returns `False` if `encounter.status in COMPLETED_CHOICES`, which blocks creating threads/messages tied to a completed encounter — verified by `test_create_note_after_encounter_complete` in test_notes_api.py, which asserts 403 for a completed encounter's thread even without an explicit `encounter` field in the message payload (the thread's own `encounter` gates via `authorize_thread_write`).

### Flows (API-level)

1. **List threads for a patient**: `GET /api/v1/patient/{patient_external_id}/thread/` — optionally `?encounter={uuid}` and/or `?encounter_isnull=true|false`. Requires `can_view_clinical_data` on patient, or (if filtering by `?encounter=`) `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` on that encounter.
2. **Create a patient-level thread** (no encounter): `POST .../thread/` with `{"title": "..."}`. Requires `can_write_patient_obj`.
3. **Create an encounter-scoped thread**: `POST .../thread/` with `{"title": "...", "encounter": "<uuid>"}`. Requires `can_update_encounter_clinical_data` on that encounter; encounter must belong to the same patient or 400 "Patient Mismatch"; encounter must exist or pydantic validator raises "Encounter not found".
4. **Retrieve a thread**: `GET .../thread/{external_id}/` — **no thread-specific authorization is enforced** beyond DRF's default `get_object` (see SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES #1).
5. **Rename a thread**: `PUT`/`PATCH .../thread/{external_id}/` with `{"title": "..."}`. Same permission logic as create, evaluated against the thread's own `encounter`/`patient`.
6. **List messages in a thread**: `GET /api/v1/patient/{patient_external_id}/thread/{thread_external_id}/note/` — same view-permission fallback logic as thread list; additionally the thread must belong to the given patient (400 otherwise).
7. **Create a message**: `POST .../note/` with `{"message": "..."}` and optionally `{"encounter": "<uuid>"}` to tag the message to a specific encounter (must match the thread's patient or 400). Requires write permission on the thread (encounter-scoped or patient-scoped, based on the thread's own `encounter`).
8. **Retrieve a message**: `GET .../note/{external_id}/` — validated to belong to the resolved thread (400 if not), but (as with threads) `get_object` lookup itself is the default DRF one, no extra authz beyond `authorize_retrieve`'s thread-membership check (no view-permission re-check at object level — see AMBIGUITIES/issues).
9. **Edit a message**: `PUT`/`PATCH .../note/{external_id}/` with `{"message": "..."}`. Only the original author (`created_by`) may edit; write permission on the thread is also required; edits append the previous message text + metadata to `message_history["history"]`.
10. **Delete thread or message**: **Not supported** — no route/action exists.

### Config that changes behavior
None found. Notes has no dedicated settings; the only behavior-affecting external factor is the generic encounter-status check (`COMPLETED_CHOICES`, from `care/emr/resources/encounter/constants.py`, used inside `can_update_encounter_clinical_data`) which blocks writes once an encounter is completed. No entries for "note"/"thread"/"message" exist in `config/settings/config.py` (confirmed via grep, zero matches).

### SUSPECTED CODE ISSUES

1. **`NoteThreadViewSet.get_object` is a stub with unenforced TODO** ([notes.py:88-90](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py#L88-L90)):
   ```python
   def get_object(self):
       # TODO Authorise Based on encounter and permission
       return super().get_object()
   ```
   This means **retrieving a single thread by ID (`GET .../thread/{id}/`) performs no authorization check at all** beyond the base DRF queryset lookup (which itself is only scoped by `patient` in `get_queryset`, and `get_queryset`'s permission gate is bypassed for direct `retrieve` because `EMRRetrieveMixin.authorize_retrieve` is not overridden in `NoteThreadViewSet` — it defaults to a no-op in `EMRRetrieveMixin.authorize_retrieve` at base.py, and `get_queryset`'s permission check only runs when `get_queryset()` is called, which it is via `get_object()`'s default DRF behavior, but that call itself is guarded by the *same* `get_queryset` permission gate — so in practice `retrieve` does inherit the list-level gate via the queryset filter). **However**, the TODO explicitly signals this is considered insufficiently fine-grained (e.g., it doesn't distinguish encounter-scoped from patient-scoped view rights at single-object granularity), which is inconsistent with the finer-grained `authorize_retrieve` used in `NoteMessageViewSet` for the same purpose.
2. **`NoteThread` model has a bare `# TODO Add organizations to further restrict access`** ([notes.py:11](../../../ohc.network/care/care/emr/models/notes.py#L11)) — confirms organization-scoped restriction (beyond patient/encounter) is acknowledged as missing.
3. **The `?encounter=` fallback authorization in both viewsets' `get_queryset` does not verify the encounter is actually associated with the thread(s)/message(s) being returned.** A user without `can_view_clinical_data` but with `can_view_encounter_clinical_data` for *some* encounter can pass any encounter's UUID they're authorized for as `?encounter=`, and if that check passes, the code proceeds to return **all threads for the patient** (`queryset.filter(patient=patient)`, not filtered by the given encounter) in `NoteThreadViewSet.get_queryset` (notes.py:104-106), or **all messages for the resolved thread** regardless of whether that thread matches the given encounter, in `NoteMessageViewSet.get_queryset` (notes.py:174-179). This looks like a genuine access-control gap: the encounter param is used only as an authorization key, not as an actual query filter tying returned data to that encounter.
4. **`NoteMessage` has no `encounter` field on the Django model** (`care/emr/models/notes.py:14-17`), yet `NoteMessageViewSet.perform_create` does `instance.encounter = encounter` (notes.py:130) when the request includes an `encounter` key. This sets an in-memory attribute that is **silently discarded** on `instance.save()` since Django will raise `AttributeError`... actually Django models allow arbitrary attribute assignment without error (it just isn't persisted/mapped to a column) — so this line executes without exception but the `encounter` value is **never saved to the database and never returned in any read spec** (`NoteMessageReadSpec` has no `encounter` field). This is dead/misleading code — it silently discards user-submitted "encounter" data on a message with no persistence and no serialization, other than being used transiently for the "Patient Mismatch" validation check.
5. **Inconsistent superuser bypass**: `PatientAccess.can_write_patient_obj` / `can_view_clinical_data` explicitly bypass for `user.is_superuser`, but the `EncounterAccess` methods used in the encounter-scoped code paths (`can_update_encounter_clinical_data`, `can_view_encounter_clinical_data`) shown do not have an explicit superuser short-circuit in the excerpts read (they call `check_permission_in_facility_organization`, whose superuser handling was not verified — see AMBIGUITIES). If that helper doesn't bypass superusers, a superuser could be denied clinical-data actions on encounter-scoped notes while always being allowed on patient-scoped notes — an inconsistency, though the test file uses `self.superuser` mainly for read-only/validation tests, not for exercising this specific gap.
6. **Message-level author restriction has no exception, not even for admins** — `authorize_update` in `NoteMessageViewSet` (notes.py:145-146) hard-codes "only the original author may edit," with no permission-based override (e.g., no facility-admin exception), which may or may not be intended.

### AMBIGUITIES / UNVERIFIED

- Whether `check_permission_in_facility_organization` / `check_permission_in_organization` (used inside `EncounterAccess` methods) contain a superuser bypass was **not verified** — I did not open `care/security/authorization/base.py` in full to confirm this, so issue #5 above is a suspicion, not a confirmed bug.
- Whether the `title` field's model-level `null=True, blank=True` (`care/emr/models/notes.py:7`) is ever actually reachable as null in practice (e.g., via `model_bakery.baker.make(... _fill_optional=True)` in tests, or via any internal/non-API code path that creates a `NoteThread` directly) was not verified — from the public API it is always required due to `Field(...)` in the pydantic spec.
- I did not verify whether pagination defaults/page size differ for notes vs. other EMR list endpoints — no notes-specific pagination class is set on either viewset, so the default DRF/EMR pagination presumably applies, but the pagination class itself wasn't traced.
- The exact wording "Cannot Update Message Created by Other User" is confirmed in code (notes.py:146) but I did not find a test in `test_notes_api.py` that specifically asserts this exact error string for a *different-user* edit attempt (the tests present for "update without permission" use an unauthenticated/no-role user, not a same-role different-user scenario) — so the behavior is verified via static code reading but not via an executed test assertion I could find.
- Whether frontend (`care_fe`) actually surfaces `message_history` in a "Notes" UI, and how the encounter-scoped vs. patient-scoped tabs map to the `?encounter=`/`encounter_isnull` filters, is **out of scope** for this backend-only research and was not investigated.

**Where you start from**

**Steps**

   - Medication Notes
   - Care Coordination
   - General Notes
   - Patient History
   - Referral Notes
   - Lab Results Discussion

- A title can hold a maximum of 255 characters.

Doctor, Nurse, Administrator, and Facility Admin hold this permission. | | Can Update a Patient's data | Lets you start a discussion on the patient profile. Staff, Doctor, Nurse, Administrator, and Facility Admin hold this permission. | ## Steps ### 1. {"method": "create", "owner": "ohcnetwork", "repo": "care_fe", "title": "Patient profile "Notes" tab has no frontend RBAC — always visible, always shows read/write UI", "body": "**Describe the bug**

The patient profile "Notes" tab does not apply any role-based access control on the frontend:

1. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx), the `getTabVisibility` switch statement (around [lines 89-107](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx#L89-L107)) has no `case "notes":`. It falls through to `default: return tab;`, so `visible` stays `undefined`. The later `.filter((tab) => tab.visible ?? true)` treats `undefined` as visible, so the Notes tab is **always shown**, regardless of the viewing user's permissions.
2. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx#L6-L12), `PatientNotesTab` renders:
   ```tsx
   <NoteManager
     canAccess={true}
     canWrite={true}
     patientId={props.patientData.id}
     encounterId={undefined}
     hideEncounterNotes={true}
   />
   ```
   Both `canAccess` and `canWrite` are hardcoded literals with no permission lookup at all, so the note composer always renders as usable regardless of the user's actual permissions.

**Contrast with the encounter-scoped Notes tab**, which does this correctly: [src/pages/Encounters/tabs/notes.tsx](src/pages/Encounters/tabs/notes.tsx) pulls `canReadSelectedEncounter` and `canWriteSelectedEncounter` from [`useEncounter()`](src/pages/Encounters/utils/EncounterProvider.tsx) and passes them straight through to `NoteManager`.

**Backend enforcement (for reference, not part of this bug — backend is not affected):**

`care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py` (`NoteThreadViewSet`) does enforce permissions correctly:
- `get_queryset` requires `can_view_clinical_data` ("Can view clinical data about patients") on the patient.
- `authorize_create` / `authorize_update` require `can_write_patient_obj` ("Can Update a Patient's data") when the thread has no encounter.

So this is **not a data-exposure hole at the API layer** — a user without permission will still get refused server-side. The impact is purely a **misleading UI**: a user without `can_view_clinical_data` (or `can_write_patient`) still sees the Notes tab and a working-looking composer, and only discovers the refusal after submitting a request that the backend rejects.

**To Reproduce**

1. Log in as a user who lacks patient clinical-data permissions on a given patient (e.g. no `can_view_clinical_data` / `can_write_patient` for that patient's organization).
2. Open that patient's profile.
3. Observe the "Notes" tab is present in the tab list and, once opened, the note composer appears fully interactive (nothing indicates the user cannot actually read/write notes).
4. Attempting to load/create a note thread fails only when the API call is made, with no prior UI indication.

**Expected behavior**

The Notes tab visibility and the `NoteManager` props should mirror what the backend enforces:
- read/visibility → gated on `can_view_clinical_data` permission (`PERMISSION_VIEW_CLINICAL_DATA` / `canViewClinicalData` in `src/common/Permissions.tsx`)
- write → gated on `can_write_patient` permission (`PERMISSION_WRITE_PATIENT` / `canWritePatient` in `src/common/Permissions.tsx`)

**Proposed fix**

1. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx), add a `case "notes": return { ...tab, visible: canViewClinicalData };` to the `getTabVisibility` switch, consistent with how `"files"` and `"clinical_history"` already gate on `canViewClinicalData`.
2. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx), derive `canAccess`/`canWrite` from patient permissions instead of hardcoding `true`. The sibling patient tabs (e.g. [Demography.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/Demography.tsx#L22-L39), [EncounterHistory.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/EncounterHistory.tsx#L24-L40), [patientUpdates.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/patientUpdates.tsx#L14-L27)) already establish the pattern: use `usePermissions()` from `@/context/PermissionContext` to get `hasPermission`, then call `getPermissions(hasPermission, patientData.permissions)` from `@/common/Permissions` to destructure `canViewClinicalData` and `canWritePatient`. `PatientNotesTab` should do the same and pass `canAccess={canViewClinicalData}` and `canWrite={canWritePatient}` to `NoteManager`.
3. Leave the encounter-scoped Notes tab (`src/pages/Encounters/tabs/notes.tsx`) unchanged — it already does this correctly.

**Additional context**

This was found via code review, not a live exploit report. No backend change is required or in scope for this issue.
"}

arguments.body:
**Describe the bug**

The patient profile "Notes" tab does not apply any role-based access control on the frontend:

1. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx), the `getTabVisibility` switch statement (around [lines 89-107](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx#L89-L107)) has no `case "notes":`. It falls through to `default: return tab;`, so `visible` stays `undefined`. The later `.filter((tab) => tab.visible ?? true)` treats `undefined` as visible, so the Notes tab is **always shown**, regardless of the viewing user's permissions.
2. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx#L6-L12), `PatientNotesTab` renders:
   ```tsx
   <NoteManager
     canAccess={true}
     canWrite={true}
     patientId={props.patientData.id}
     encounterId={undefined}
     hideEncounterNotes={true}
   />
   ```
   Both `canAccess` and `canWrite` are hardcoded literals with no permission lookup at all, so the note composer always renders as usable regardless of the user's actual permissions.

**Contrast with the encounter-scoped Notes tab**, which does this correctly: [src/pages/Encounters/tabs/notes.tsx](src/pages/Encounters/tabs/notes.tsx) pulls `canReadSelectedEncounter` and `canWriteSelectedEncounter` from [`useEncounter()`](src/pages/Encounters/utils/EncounterProvider.tsx) and passes them straight through to `NoteManager`.

**Backend enforcement (for reference, not part of this bug — backend is not affected):**

`care/emr/api/viewsets/notes.py` (`NoteThreadViewSet`) does enforce permissions correctly:
- `get_queryset` requires `can_view_clinical_data` ("Can view clinical data about patients") on the patient.
- `authorize_create` / `authorize_update` require `can_write_patient_obj` ("Can Update a Patient's data") when the thread has no encounter.

So this is **not a data-exposure hole at the API layer** — a user without permission will still get refused server-side. The impact is purely a **misleading UI**: a user without `can_view_clinical_data` (or `can_write_patient`) still sees the Notes tab and a working-looking composer, and only discovers the refusal after submitting a request that the backend rejects.

**To Reproduce**

1. Log in as a user who lacks patient clinical-data permissions on a given patient (e.g. no `can_view_clinical_data` / `can_write_patient` for that patient's organization).
2. Open that patient's profile.
3. Observe the "Notes" tab is present in the tab list and, once opened, the note composer appears fully interactive (nothing indicates the user cannot actually read/write notes).
4. Attempting to load/create a note thread fails only when the API call is made, with no prior UI indication.

**Expected behavior**

The Notes tab visibility and the `NoteManager` props should mirror what the backend enforces:
- read/visibility → gated on `can_view_clinical_data` permission (`PERMISSION_VIEW_CLINICAL_DATA` / `canViewClinicalData` in `src/common/Permissions.tsx`)
- write → gated on `can_write_patient` permission (`PERMISSION_WRITE_PATIENT` / `canWritePatient` in `src/common/Permissions.tsx`)

**Proposed fix**

1. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/index.tsx), add a `case "notes": return { ...tab, visible: canViewClinicalData };` to the `getTabVisibility` switch, consistent with how `"files"` and `"clinical_history"` already gate on `canViewClinicalData`.
2. In [src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/PatientNotes.tsx), derive `canAccess`/`canWrite` from patient permissions instead of hardcoding `true`. The sibling patient tabs (e.g. [Demography.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/Demography.tsx#L22-L39), [EncounterHistory.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/EncounterHistory.tsx#L24-L40), [patientUpdates.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/patientUpdates.tsx#L14-L27)) already establish the pattern: use `usePermissions()` from `@/context/PermissionContext` to get `hasPermission`, then call `getPermissions(hasPermission, patientData.permissions)` from `@/common/Permissions` to destructure `canViewClinicalData` and `canWritePatient`. `PatientNotesTab` should do the same and pass `canAccess={canViewClinicalData}` and `canWrite={canWritePatient}` to `NoteManager`.
3. Leave the encounter-scoped Notes tab (`src/pages/Encounters/tabs/notes.tsx`) unchanged — it already does this correctly.

**Additional context**

This was found via code review, not a live exploit report. No backend change is required or in scope for this issue.

data.content:
Review complete. All four files edited in place.

## `concept.md`

| Issue | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| FHIR statement read awkwardly ("No FHIR R5 resource backs it" — passive-ish, reversed subject) | Reworded to "Clinical Notes is a Care feature for staff collaboration. Care does not map Clinical Notes to an FHIR R5 resource." No FHIR link added. |
| Terminology drift: "A discussion is a titled **thread** of messages" | "A discussion groups related messages under one title. A message is one entry in a discussion." |
| Permanence section used "You cannot delete…" (a capability claim) | Changed to the observed UI fact: "Care shows no way to delete a discussion / a message." |
| **Factual error — roles.** Encounter clinical-data permissions grant to Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Facility Admin — *not* Administrator. Patient rows omitted Admin. | Encounter rows: Doctor, Nurse, Admin, Facility Admin. "Can view clinical data about patients": Staff, Doctor, Nurse, Admin, Facility Admin. "Can Update a Patient's data": Staff, Doctor, Nurse, Administrator, Admin, Facility Admin. |
| **Factual error — "complete".** Writes are blocked for four statuses, not just Completed. | "If the encounter is closed… Care treats an encounter as closed when its status is Completed, Cancelled, Discontinued, or Entered in error." |

Verified as correct, left unchanged: 255-character title limit, 20 messages per page, newest-first ordering, no attachments, no mentions, missing Status section, all four Related links resolve (including `../Encounter/concept.md`), centered H1.

## `flows/1. Start a discussion.md`

| Issue | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| **Invented content.** The "What it captures" column described the seven suggested titles; those meanings are not in the codebase. | Table deleted. Replaced with a plain bullet list of the seven titles, verbatim and in source order. |
| "A discussion is a titled **thread**" in Overview | Reworded to "groups related messages under one title". |
| "encounter that is complete" | Rewritten to the four closed statuses. |
| Role lists in Permissions table | Corrected as above. |
| "On a small screen, select **New Thread**" — location omitted; the control is in the bottom navigation bar | "…select **New Thread** at the bottom of the screen." |
| "A suggested title leaves the list after a discussion in this list uses it" — passive/awkward | "Care removes a suggested title from the list when a discussion in this list already uses that title." |
| Chained instruction: "Care shows '…' **and** does not create the discussion" | Split into two sentences. |
| Expected Outcome mentioned renaming a discussion | Removed per your rule 2; the note now reads "Care shows no way to delete a discussion after you create it." |

Kept: the quoted on-screen strings "New Thread", "Thread with this title already exists", "Failed to create thread", "Thread created successfully", "Please enter a custom title for thread", "Choose a template or enter a custom title", "Enter discussion title…". All verified in `en.json`.

## `flows/2. Post a message to a discussion.md`

| Issue | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Data-model phrasing: "A discussion exists in the list…" / "If no discussion exists" | "Someone started a discussion in the list that you look at. If the list holds no discussion, …" |
| "the encounter is not complete" | Rewritten to the four closed statuses. |
| Role lists | Corrected as above. |
| "On a small screen, open the list first" — vague | "…select **Threads** at the bottom of the screen." |
| **Factual error.** "Select the author's name or picture to open that user's profile" — only the avatar is a link; the name is plain text. | "Select the author's picture to open that user's profile." |
| "Caution: … Care gives no message on screen" — awkward, and Caution is not warranted | "Note: If Care cannot send the message, Care shows no error. Look at the discussion to make sure that your message is there." |
| Expected Outcome mentioned changing a message after sending | Removed per your rule 2; kept only "Care shows no way to delete a message." |

Verified and kept: `Shift`+`Enter` sends on non-touch devices, the send button on touch, auto-expanding input, Markdown rendering, auto-selection of the most recent discussion, 20-message paging, hover tooltip on the timestamp.

## `flows/3. Find discussions for a patient or an encounter.md`

| Issue | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Link text "clinical notes" lowercase, inconsistent with the module name | "[Clinical Notes](../concept.md)" |
| Role lists (also a malformed list: "Staff, Doctor, Nurse, Administrator, Facility Admin" with no "and") | Corrected to "Staff, Doctor, Nurse, Admin, and Facility Admin" and "Doctor, Nurse, Admin, and Facility Admin". |
| **Factual error.** "select the button above the messages" — the mobile control is in the bottom bar. | "select **Threads** at the bottom of the screen." |

Verified and kept: the Notes tab visibility note is accurate (the tab renders only when the user can read patient clinical data or encounter clinical data), no search box or filter exists, "No discussions yet" empty state, most-recent-first ordering.

## Cross-cutting checks

- **H1 centered HTML** — present in all four files, unchanged.
- **Links** — all resolve on disk: `../concept.md`, `./flows/1.%20Start%20a%20discussion.md`, `./flows/2.%20Post%20a%20message%20to%20a%20discussion.md`, `./flows/3.%20Find%20discussions%20for%20a%20patient%20or%20an%20encounter.md`, `./1.%20…`, `./2.%20…`, `./3.%20…`, `../Encounter/concept.md`. Spaces encoded as `%20`. Concept ↔ flow links are bidirectional.
- **File naming** — all three flows use `<n>. <Sentence case>.md`. Ordering (start → post → find) is sensible.
- **Terminology** — "thread" now appears only inside quoted on-screen strings and UI labels ("New Thread", "Threads", "Thread with this title already exists", "Select or create a thread…", "Failed to create thread"). Prose uses discussion / message / Notes tab / Discussions panel throughout.
- **No codebase literals** — no enum values, slugs, paths, or endpoints in any file. Permission names are the human-readable ones from the backend `Permission` definitions.
- **Keyboard shortcut** — `g` then `n` is defined only in the encounter shortcut group. Both flows that mention it scope it to the encounter. Correct.

## Open issues for you
